result.killer: Two things kill it. (1) The market is far smaller than claimed. Parliament narrowed the bill: own-use residential purchases are exempt, as are deals under CHF 5m paid through banks, and the Finance Minister said 99% of property transactions are unaffected (Blick). (2) A Swiss vendor already covers the reform. Legalian (legalian.ch) markets a GwG platform at the 1 Oct 2026 reform, aimed at "lawyers, notaries, fiduciaries and other advisors", with Real Estate as a target sector. It offers register and UBO searches, PEP and sanctions screening, client questionnaires, risk scoring, signed reporting packages and ongoing monitoring, and integrates with Vertec, the practice software common among Swiss fiduciaries. It also states the 1 Dec 2026 SRO deadline.
result.reason: The SRO deadline is confirmed. WEKA (a Burkhalter law-firm article) and Legalian both say advisers active on 1 Oct 2026 must apply to an SRO by 1 Dec 2026. The thresholds for professional activity are CHF 50k revenue, more than 20 clients or more than CHF 2m in transactions. But the exemptions for own-use residential deals and bank-paid deals under CHF 5m leave about 1% of property deals in scope. Those are mostly commercial deals, investment deals and deals with unusual payment routes, handled by few and often larger brokers. Fiduciaries and company-formation advisers are already served by Legalian (with Vertec integration), Zyphe and law-firm services. A broker-specific pack would be a thin wedge in a tiny niche. Unverified: SRO fees and whether SROs supply their own tools.

result.competitor: Nothing found that is specific to Swiss real estate brokers or advisers. Generic Swiss AML/KYC software exists: Zyphe (ID checks, PEP and sanctions screening, beneficial-owner lookup, MROS report drafts), KYC360 and PXL GWG Ident (aimed at banks and fintechs), plus Goldblum's outsourced compliance officer and SRO-audit readiness service. The 11 FINMA-recognised SROs (e.g. VQF, ARIF) set member rules and forms, and may supply templates. Whether any SRO offers software, and which SROs accept brokers, was not verified. No SVIT SRO solution found.
result.duty: Revised GwG (Art. 2 para. 3bis/3ter, Art. 8b-8c, Art. 12) and GwV (Art. 12f, 12g), in force 1 Oct 2026. Professional advisers who help third parties with the financial side of property purchases or sales, or with setting up, administering or trading non-operating entities, must: identify the client and the beneficial owner; establish the purpose of the transaction; clarify higher-risk cases; document and keep records for 10 years; report suspicions to MROS; and have training, internal controls and sanctions measures. These duties apply from 1 Oct 2026 with no transition. Advisers already active must file an SRO membership application by 1 Dec 2026, and new advisers within 2 months of starting. Until the SRO decides, existing relationships may only be continued. An external audit firm checks compliance, at the member's cost. Without a timely application or with a refusal, the activity must stop, and SROs can impose sanctions. Criminal penalty amounts were not verified. FINMA-supervised advisers must notify FINMA via EHP by 1 Dec 2026. Exemptions: owner-occupied residential property; deals under CHF 5m paid only through regulated banks or intermediaries; family and inheritance transfers; intra-group services; agricultural land for owner-cultivators; and others.
result.market: Not quantified. No count of brokers or advisers in scope was found. The government's cost study (BASS for SIF) reportedly contains a headcount estimate, but it was not reached. The exemptions (own-use homes; bank-paid deals under CHF 5m) remove much of the ordinary residential brokerage. Brokers would still need to screen each deal to decide whether it is in scope. The likely buyers are brokers handling investment or commercial property, high-value deals, and fiduciaries or company-formation and domicile providers. For context, about 485,000 companies are on the commercial register (these are the companies themselves, not the advisers).
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. FINMA confirms the revised GwG/GwV took effect on 1 Oct 2026. According to BDO (citing Art. 12g nGwV) and WEKA, advisers already active must apply to an SRO by 1 Dec 2026. KYC, beneficial-owner, record-keeping, MROS-reporting and training duties apply with no transition period, and records must be kept 10 years. I found no broker-specific Swiss tool. What exists is generic financial-intermediary KYC/AML software (Zyphe, KYC360, PXL GWG Ident) and outsourced compliance (Goldblum). The market is narrow because of broad exemptions: owner-occupied homes, and deals under CHF 5m paid through banks. That makes per-deal scope screening plus KYC a real but small niche. The number of brokers affected was not found. SROs will likely supply forms, and the SVIT position was not found.

result.competitor: Reporting: the free official platform cooling-reg.ch, run by Lombardi SA for BAFU, handles registration, changes, deregistration and vignette orders, works on mobile, and paper is still accepted. Its BAFU page mentions no API and no electronic logbook. This settles the unresolved Lombardi vs. cooling-reg.ch question in the claim: they are the same service. The reporting office also sells the paper logbook and vignette. I found no Swiss-specific digital logbook in German or French searches. Foreign F-gas logbook tools exist (Refcom/Joblogic and FGASmanager in the UK, GoCanvas templates), and general trade software such as STREIT (Germany) is used by refrigeration firms. I did not check SVK/ASF tools or Swiss field-service suites.
result.duty: ChemRRV Annex 2.10 (Swiss federal law, in force). Owners of stationary systems with more than 3 kg of refrigerant must make sure a maintenance logbook (Wartungsheft) is kept, with the owner's name in it. After each job the technician records the date, the work done, the leak-check result, the refrigerant type and quantity removed or added, the firm and a signature. Leak checks are required at least at every intervention and maintenance visit for systems over 3 kg (ozone-depleting or air-stable refrigerants) or over 5 t CO2-eq. Leaks must be repaired without delay. Commissioning, changes and decommissioning must be reported to the BAFU reporting office. The leak-check frequency comes from the French BAFU page and guidance search results; I could not open the 2025 BAFU guidance itself (HTTP 502). The Federal Council decision of 29 Oct 2025 (AS 2025 747), effective 1 Jan 2027 for import and 1 Jul 2027 for supply to third parties, mainly adds bans on placing certain air-stable-refrigerant systems on the market. Search summaries described no logbook change, but I did not read the legal text. Not found: no specific fine amounts. Basel-Stadt and national campaigns found many faults (two thirds of 211 systems flagged nationally). FWS (fws.ch) disputes whether the maintenance duty applies to heat pumps.
result.market: BAFU statistics (data to 2022, published May 2024): about 230,000 systems over 3 kg in operation, with more than 13,000 new ones a year, and heat pumps growing fastest. I did not find the number of distinct owners or of refrigeration and heat-pump service firms. The likely buyers are service firms rather than the many owners, and that is a few hundred to low thousands of firms (my estimate, not verified).
result.reason: The duty is real, but the gap is narrow. Owners of systems over 3 kg must keep a maintenance logbook, have leak checks done at every intervention and maintenance visit, and report commissioning, changes and decommissioning (ChemRRV Annex 2.10). The free BAFU platform cooling-reg.ch, run by Lombardi SA, already handles the reporting. No source showed it has an electronic logbook, and I found no Swiss logbook app. The 2027 amendment mainly bans placing certain systems on the market, so it brings no new logbook deadline. Service firms, not owners, write the logbook and probably use field-service software. Owners are unlikely to pay, there is no fixed check interval, and FWS disputes the duty for heat pumps. I made 8 searches, 2 over the budget of 6.

result.competitor: I found no Swiss product marketed as SWK-compliant or offering an SWK export. The SWK portal is free and the annual return is entered by hand (two figures). Generic ERPs (Abacus at Weinkellereien Aarau) and stock systems are accepted in place of Kellerbuch cards. Wine-specific software exists, such as BOXXER VINO (Medialine, a digital Kellerbuch). Valais provides gateways from cellar software into e-Vendanges, so Swiss cellar-software vendors exist, but none are named on the cantonal page. Harvest control goes through free state portals (e-Vendanges, Agate/Gelan eAttest). Not reached: Romandie cellar-software vendors that have e-Vendanges gateways, and whether the SWK portal has an upload or API.
result.duty: Swiss Weinverordnung (SR 916.140) Art. 33–41: anyone trading wine commercially must notify the SWK before starting (Art. 34 exemptions apply). Cellar accounting must be kept continuously, one card per wine and vintage; a warehouse or ERP system may replace the cards. Every year the 31 Dec inventory and the litres sold must be entered in the SWK customer account by 31 Jan, with no reminder sent. Records are kept 10 years under the OR. Inspections are risk-based, about every 6–8 years. Firms selling only labelled bottles to end consumers can get simplified accounting (two annual lists, no inventory) after their first inspection. Penalties are mainly administrative orders, such as backdated cellar accounting (BVGer B-4173/2022, 2024); I found no fine amounts. Separately, cellars do their own harvest control: Valais via e-Vendanges by 15 Nov (late harvest 28 Feb), and German-speaking cantons via eAttest on Agate/Gelan.
result.market: The SWK controlled 1,480 wine-trade businesses in 2017 and 1,336 in 2018 (SWK activity report via 1815.ch). From 2019 about 1,100 self-cellarers (Selbsteinkellerer) also came under the SWK. Statista has the registered count to Dec 2024 behind a paywall, so the current total is unverified; a rough estimate is 3,000–4,000 registered businesses. The BLW Weinjahr 2022 PDF returned a 502 error.
result.reason: The duty is real. Weinverordnung SR 916.140, Art. 33–41, requires SWK notification and continuous Kellerbuch records. The 31 Dec inventory and litres sold go into the SWK customer account by 31 Jan. In 2024 the Federal Administrative Court ordered cellar accounting backdated to 2019. No Swiss tool specific to SWK turned up. But the annual return is only two figures entered by hand, and the SWK accepts any ERP or stock system in place of paper cards. Small bottle sellers can get simplified accounting, and inspections come every 6–8 years. Valais offers gateways from cellar software into e-Vendanges, so cellar-software vendors exist. About 1,480 firms were controlled in 2017, plus about 1,100 self-cellarers from 2019. Pain and willingness to pay look low.

result.competitor: Brunner Informatik's 'Meldewesen M2' suite has a product made for control bodies: infraDATA express, described as 'Software zur effizienten Abwicklung von Elektro-Kontrollen'. Its product page says it tracks open jobs and their due steps, sets appointments with a calendar per employee, and keeps an order list. It generates the Sicherheitsnachweis, Messprotokoll (test record), inspection report, quote and invoice with one click. It can take data from the measuring device, works offline and sends forms straight to the network operator. Brunner's ElektroForm EVU / infraDATA EVU covers the network operators' side, including reminders. ElektroForm online is already used for submissions, e.g. in the ewz (Zurich) network area. A related gap: on-device reminders to the owner are not explicitly listed for infraDATA express.
result.duty: Real and in force under the Swiss NIV (SR 734.27), Art. 32 and 36–37. Owners must have their installations inspected every 1, 5, 10 or 20 years, plus at a change of ownership when the 10/20-year period has run at least 5 years. An independent control body or an accredited inspection body issues the Sicherheitsnachweis (safety certificate). The network operator must send a written reminder at least 6 months before the deadline. After the reminders are ignored, enforcement passes to ESTI (the federal electrical inspectorate). The legal duty falls on the owner. The control body is a service provider, not the party with the duty. Penalty: ESTI enforcement, with orders and fees, up to cutting off the power supply (ESTI publication 2017-12 'Unterbrechen der Stromzufuhr').
result.market: ESTI's NIV annual report for 2019 counted 2,568 valid inspection permits (Kontrollbewilligungen): 849 individuals and 1,719 firms. The figure has been stable at about 2,500–2,650 since 2013. Not every permit holder is an independent control body. No more recent count was found. The secondary buyers, property owners, are many, but network operators already remind them for free.
result.reason: The duty is real, recurring and enforced (NIV Art. 36). But it sits on owners, while the proposed buyer, independent control bodies, numbers only about 2,500 permit holders (ESTI 2019). The claim that no control-body software exists is wrong. Brunner Informatik's infraDATA express is sold to control bodies for running electrical inspections: job tracking with due steps, per-employee calendars, one-click Sicherheitsnachweis and test records, data from measuring devices, and direct submission to network operators. The same vendor's ElektroForm already dominates installer reporting to network operators (known idea K10) and has network-operator modules. Owner reminders are already done for free by network operators. The market is small and the incumbent is entrenched, which leaves only niche differentiation.

Duty is real but soft. The Arbeitsgesetz excludes private households (Art. 2 Abs. 1 lit. g ArG). Art. 359 Abs. 2 OR makes cantons issue a NAV for household staff. The SECO Modell-NAV is a minimum standard that cantons are expected to adopt, not a binding federal rule. It has Dokumentationspflichten, but I could not read the PDF text (compressed), so frequency, penalty and per-canton adoption are unverified. Cantons have differing rules (SZ 45h, GR 44h). Zug revised its NAV on 1 Sept 2025 with working-time documentation. A NAV breach has no direct fine. No Swiss live-in time-recording tool was found (generic apps only: bexio, tagwerCH). Market size was not found; the buyers are fragmented households with low willingness to pay.

The duty is real. Drinking water counts as food, so suppliers must run a risk-based self-control (HACCP-type) concept with sampling under SVGW W1. They must also inform consumers at least annually. Cantons check this (FR, ZH, SG). I did not confirm penalties or the exact LMG article. Market: about 3000 public supplies, but the figure comes from an old gwa 2009 source. The SVGW survey covers roughly 670. Many are municipal and are consolidating. Competition: the DQW tool from the claim (not re-verified by my searches) plus free canton templates, the Eawag database and the ZH Trinkwasser Map. Buyers are mostly municipalities with small budgets, so willingness to pay is low and sales are slow. Weak fit for a solo founder.

The duty is real but fragmented. Kurtaxe and Beherbergungsabgabe are set by canton and commune, and private hosts are covered (Bern law clarified 2014 per law.ch). Schaffhausen also requires a guest register for private hosts. The core job is partly handled already. Airbnb collects automatically under about 10 agreements, the latest St. Gallen in July 2025. Chekin, Lodgify and Guesty handle guest reporting. Commune rules and portals differ, so one product is hard to build. Hosts pay little, and reaching them commune by commune is slow. I did not verify host counts, per-commune filing workload or the Ettiswil and Ufhusen 2027 rules. Several sources date from 2014-2019.

The duty is real. Under the Thurgau tax practice text and the Zurich ELM page, the employer (the SSL, Schuldner der steuerbaren Leistung) must settle withholding tax with the canton. In Thurgau this is monthly. The employer is liable regardless of fault, and Zurich pays a 2% collection commission that can be cut. Competition already covers the core job. Swissdec-certified payroll handles ELM Quellensteuer. Some cantons offer a free web application for employers whose software lacks ELM (Solothurn, in a 2016 document). Cantonal paper and portal routes also exist. This overlaps known idea K08. No register count was found. Fine amounts were not found either. A standalone product is weak.

result.duty: GSchG Art. 22 periodic tank inspection (about every 10 years), cantonal vignette and Kontrollheft rules
result.market: not_reached: no register count found; the firm list is held by CITEC Suisse
result.reason: Duty is real: GSchG Art. 22 (regular inspection, about every 10 years by a specialist firm). Valais vignette for tanks over 450 L since 1 Jan 2025, valid 10 years, and suppliers may only fill vignette-marked tanks. Thurgau bans filling without a valid Kontrollheft and requires firms to report to the canton. I did not check the GSchG text or the penalty directly. No dedicated tank-register software or vendor turned up in 3 searches, and no national tank count. Weak case: the cycle is 10 years, so frequency is low. Volumes are shrinking with heat pumps. Rules differ by canton, so the MVP is fragmented. The buyer pool of CITEC-listed firms and oil dealers is small, and the pain is modest. Not checked: whether cantons run firm portals, and Valais dealer lookup.

Duty is real and in force: TJPG and its ordinance took effect 1 Oct 2026 (admin.ch). Non-listed AG, GmbH and Genossenschaften must report beneficial owners via EasyGov.swiss. Changes are due within 1 month. Fines run up to CHF 500k for intentional breaches. Transition deadlines per bexio and Grant Thornton: AG with ordinary audit end Dec 2026, GmbH with ordinary audit Jan 2027, AG without ordinary audit Feb 2027, other GmbH Mar/Apr 2027, up to 2 years if owners are already in the commercial register. Foundations and associations are excluded (Forvis Mazars). The state portal is free. I found no dedicated software, but fiduciaries will bundle filing, and it is mostly a one-off with few later changes. No company count found (roughly 300k+ entities is my unverified estimate). Weak recurring revenue, a short window.

Duty is weaker than claimed. Per BAZG, a domestic LE is issued only when a supplier chooses to pass on preferential origin (VAU, 23 May 2012). It is not mandatory for every firm, and it is usable only for domestic supply. It cannot be used for CH-EU cross-border trade. Retention is 3 years (5 for Korea/India); long-term LE up to 2 years. No fixed frequency or penalty found; the exporter bears the risk of a wrong LE. Competition: the AEB supplier portal exists, but its Swiss coverage is unchecked. No Swiss-specific product, ERP module or Handelskammer service was found, but only 3 searches were run. The number of small exporters was not found. Bilaterale III effect not checked. The niche is narrow, optional and fragmented, so the score stays at 3.

The duty is real: DZV/ÖLN, annual structure-data survey, Suisse-Bilanz, and a Behandlungsjournal (Agridea says 3 years retention, not the 5 claimed). But the core job is already covered. The cantons' NikA/LAWIS (Softec) portal is free and state-run. Barto, backed by Agridea, Identitas and Fenaco, offers a Suisse-Bilanz module and 365FarmNet, plus a "Control Dossier" module that won an innovation prize at Suisse Tier 2025 for inspection prep. Arenenberg lists several digital record-keeping tools (e.g. AGROPLUS). Whether any tool has a Behandlungsjournal was not confirmed. Not checked: NikA vendor interface, 2027 changes, farm count (roughly 45-48k farms, from memory only). The buyer is hard to reach and has low willingness to pay, because the incumbents are co-op-backed.
